title: Cross-Sectional Backscattered Electron Imaging of Mechanically Polished Organic-Inorganic Perovskite Photovoltaics
content: Organic-inorganic perovskites are an emerging class of thin film photovoltaic (PV) materials. Direct characterization of perovskite PVs is a challenge because perovskites are damaged by electron beams [1], ion beams [2], and environmental stressors (e.g., water, oxygen, heat, etc.) [3], giving rise to potential data misinterpretation—it can be difficult to deconvolute changes in the perovskite structure due to experimental conditions and damage from the characterization technique itself, particularly in cross-sectional analysis. Despite this challenge, elemental analysis of perovskite PV cross-sections is pivotal for understanding the origins of perovskite instability, degradation products, and interfacial phenomena. However, elemental analysis using energy dispersive x-ray spectroscopy (EDS) in scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is limited for thin film perovskites due to high currents and acquisition times that damage the perovskite, as well as < 100 nm features of interest which are below the detectability of SEM-EDS.
